feed.title: Backend, API & System Design — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: An annotated directory of links on software, AI, security and science. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Any API
entry.summary: A directory gathering the docs and console of hundreds of public APIs in one place. Unlike individual API sites you can try them all in a common interface.

entry.title: Awesome CakePHP
entry.summary: A list of plugins and resources for the CakePHP framework.

entry.title: Awesome Dash
entry.summary: A resource list for Dash, building data dashboards with Python.

entry.title: Awesome DDD
entry.summary: A list of resources, books and samples for domain-driven design (DDD), CQRS and event sourcing. Unlike general architecture lists it focuses on these three connected approaches.

entry.title: Awesome Deno
entry.summary: A resource list for Deno, a security- and TypeScript-focused alternative to Node. Unlike Node lists it gathers modules specific to this secure runtime.

entry.title: Awesome Directus
entry.summary: A resource list for Directus, the headless CMS offering a real-time API and dashboard.

entry.title: Awesome Drupal
entry.summary: A list of modules and resources for Drupal, the PHP-based CMS.

entry.title: Awesome FastAPI
entry.summary: A list of plugins, examples and tutorials for FastAPI, Python’s fast web framework. Unlike the official docs it gathers community libraries and production examples.

entry.title: Awesome Fiber
entry.summary: A resource list for Fiber, a fast web framework for Go.

entry.title: Awesome Firebase
entry.summary: A resource list for Firebase, Google’s app-development platform.

entry.title: Awesome Integration
entry.summary: A resource list for linking different IT systems together (integration).

entry.title: Awesome Laravel
entry.summary: A list of packages and resources for Laravel, PHP’s most popular framework.

entry.title: Awesome Low Code
entry.summary: A list of platforms letting business professionals build apps with little code.

entry.title: Awesome Magento 2
entry.summary: A resource list for Magento 2, the open-source e-commerce platform built with PHP.

entry.title: Awesome Node-RED
entry.summary: A resource list for Node-RED, wiring hardware and services together visually.

entry.title: Awesome Node.js
entry.summary: A list organising Node.js packages and resources by topic. Unlike an npm search it is a curated, quality-checked starting point.

entry.title: Awesome PHP
entry.summary: A list gathering PHP libraries, frameworks and tools by topic. Unlike a Packagist search it is curated and organised around modern PHP practice.

entry.title: Awesome Plone
entry.summary: A list of add-ons and resources for Plone, the open-source Python CMS.

entry.title: Awesome Prisma
entry.summary: A resource list for Prisma, the ORM turning a database into a type-safe client.

entry.title: Awesome Serverless
entry.summary: A resource list for serverless computing and architecture.

entry.title: Awesome Software Architecture
entry.summary: A list of resources for designing and documenting software architecture. Unlike a single book it gathers patterns, case studies and tools together, topic by topic.

entry.title: Awesome Symfony
entry.summary: A list of bundles and resources for the Symfony PHP framework.

entry.title: Awesome Vapor
entry.summary: A resource list for Vapor, server-side development in Swift.

entry.title: Convex
entry.summary: A backend platform folding the database, server functions and real-time subscriptions into one product. Where Firebase has you write rules, here queries are TypeScript functions with real transactional guarantees — document flexibility without giving up consistency.

entry.title: Free Public APIs
entry.summary: A directory of over three hundred free public APIs, each carrying a liveness status and a last-checked date. That is what separates it from the old awesome-list compilations: it actually keeps scanning whether the APIs still answer.

entry.title: Porkbun
entry.summary: An ICANN-accredited domain registrar where WHOIS privacy, SSL and email forwarding are included rather than upsold. What separates it from the GoDaddy school is that renewal prices stay close to the first-year price instead of tripling.

entry.title: High Scalability
entry.summary: An archive of architecture write-ups spanning fifteen-plus years. The old posts are dated in technology but still read for how scaling pressure was actually met.

entry.title: System Design One
entry.summary: Breaks down real company architectures as case studies with actual numbers and the trade-offs taken. That concreteness is what separates it from abstract write-ups.

entry.title: Martin Fowler · Architecture
entry.summary: Martin Fowler’s canonical collection of essays and patterns on software architecture. Unlike scattered blogs it gives the most-cited definition of concepts like microservices and event sourcing.

entry.title: Webhook.site
entry.summary: Hands you a URL instantly and shows every request that arrives, headers included. Against running a local server behind a tunnel it needs no setup — the shortest way to see what a webhook actually sends.

entry.title: Stripe
entry.summary: Payment infrastructure whose documentation is treated as an industry benchmark — test cards, webhook retry logic and idempotency keys all worked through with examples.

entry.title: GraphQL
entry.summary: The client declares which fields it wants, so over- and under-fetching are solved at the schema level. The cost is that caching and rate limiting get harder than in REST.

entry.title: Refactoring Guru
entry.summary: Presents each design pattern as a diagram, a realistic scenario and code — in six languages. An accessible counterpart to the Gang of Four book’s difficult prose.

entry.title: Express
entry.summary: Node’s minimal framework, whose middleware model became the ecosystem’s shared vocabulary. That it has barely changed in years is both its strength and its weakness.

entry.title: WordPress Developer
entry.summary: The plugin and theme development reference. The hook system is the one concept that explains all of WordPress, and nothing falls into place until you have it.

entry.title: Laracasts
entry.summary: The main video resource for the Laravel ecosystem, covering the architectural decisions the docs leave out. One site carrying an ecosystem’s training is unusual.

entry.title: Laravel
entry.summary: Queues, scheduler, broadcasting and testing tools live in the core. Against PHP’s dated reputation, the developer experience here is ahead of most modern frameworks.

entry.title: PHP: The Right Way
entry.summary: Collects current PHP practice — Composer, PSR standards, prepared statements. A corrective to the old `mysql_*` examples still circulating online.

entry.title: Flask
entry.summary: A deliberately small core — routing and templating, no ORM or auth. You choose the pieces, which also means choosing them again on every project.

entry.title: PHP El Kitabı (Türkçe)
entry.summary: The primary function reference. The user notes below each page are sometimes more useful than the doc and sometimes decade-old bad advice — check the dates.
